paragraph: Leonia's single-family market is the whole story right now: 22 sales over six months at a median of $887,500, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.0385, and a median of 16 days on market. Roughly 68 percent of those homes sold above asking. That is a real seller's market, with plenty of multiple offer situations behind those numbers. Prices ran from $570,000 to $2,200,000, so the median is the better guide than the range. Condos and townhouses are a much smaller and slower slice, 7 sales at a median of $460,000, a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00, nothing above asking, and a median of 54 days on market. Nothing is being bid up in that tier, and you'll have more room to negotiate. On the monthly series, no single month clears five closings, so it's too thin to read a trend from. July was the strongest month on both count and median, which fits the normal early-to-mid-summer peak. If Leonia follows the usual seasonal arc, expect closings and medians to ease through fall. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle and lower price point of a condo.
